figures.title: The sinusoidal ladder: angle per position and frequency
figures.caption: A heatmap of the sinusoidal encoding's angle. Each row is a position p, each column a dimension pair i, and the cell is pθ_i mod 2π, where θ_i = 10000^(−2i/d) and the two slots at that pair are its sine and cosine. The geometric ladder is visible as columns of different slope: the fastest pair wraps every 2π positions, the slowest takes about 10000·2π. The angles are illustrative, computed from the chapter's formula for d_model = 512; the chapter prints the formula, the wavelength ladder, and the p = 1 to p = 2 rotation, not this grid.
figures.alt: An 8 by 4 matrix of angles in radians. Rows are positions 0 to 7, columns are pairs 0 to 3. Column 0 advances 1 radian per position and wraps from 6 to 0.72 at the last row. Column 1 advances 0.965, column 2 0.931, column 3 0.898. The note prints the offset example: at p = 1 the pair (sin 1, cos 1) is (0.841, 0.540), and the k = 1 rotation gives (0.908, −0.415) = (sin 2, cos 2).

data.note: Angles in radians, pθ_i mod 2π with θ_i = 10000^(−2i/512), for d_model = 512 and four pairs. θ_0 = 1, θ_1 = 0.9647, θ_2 = 0.9306, θ_3 = 0.8977; the full ladder runs to a wavelength of about 10000·2π. At p = 1 the pair (sin 1, cos 1) is (0.841, 0.540); the k = 1 rotation [[0.540, 0.841], [−0.841, 0.540]] gives (0.908, −0.415) = (sin 2, cos 2).

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to walk the frequency ladder, then the p = 1 to p = 2 rotation.

steps.label: Pair i = 0 advances θ_0 = 1 radian per position and wraps every 2π.
Pair i = 1 advances θ_1 = 0.9647 radians per position.
Pair i = 3 advances θ_3 = 0.8977; the slowest pair needs about 10000·2π positions per turn.

figures.title: Two ways to put position into the score
figures.caption: RoPE rotates each query/key pair by an angle proportional to position, so the dot product depends only on the offset i − j; the absolute positions cancel. ALiBi adds no positional vector: it subtracts a per-head penalty m_h|i − j|, with eight slopes from 1/2 to 1/256. RoPE's base 10000 is the extension knob; NTK-aware scaling raises it to 20,220 for d = 128 and s = 2, and YaRN multiplies the logits by 0.967 at s = 2 and 0.910 at s = 8.
figures.alt: Two aligned panels. Left, RoPE: theta_m = 10000 to the minus 2m over d; q at i becomes cos i theta, sin i theta; k at j becomes cos j theta, sin j theta; their dot product is cos of (i minus j) theta; absolute positions cancel; the cached k is already rotated. Right, ALiBi: m_h = 2 to the minus 8h over n; eight heads have slopes 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32, 1/64, 1/128 and 1/256; the penalty is m_h times |i minus j|; m = 1/2 gives 50 at 100 tokens, m = 1/256 gives 0.39; there is no positional vector and no base knob.

panels.title: RoPE: rotate q and k by position
items: q at i → (cos iθ, sin iθ)
k at j → (cos jθ, sin jθ)
panels.note: Base 10000 is the knob: NTK-aware scaling gives 20,220 at d = 128 and s = 2; YaRN multiplies logits by 0.967 at s = 2 and 0.910 at s = 8.

panels.title: ALiBi: subtract m_h |i − j|
items: no positional vector, no base knob
panels.note: The penalty grows linearly, so far scores go to negative infinity with no periodic ambiguity.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to rotate the query and key, then compare the ALiBi penalty.

steps.label: Each pair m rotates at θ_m = 10000^(−2m/d).
Rotate q at position i: (1, 0) becomes (cos iθ, sin iθ); rotate k at j the same way.
The pair dot is cos((i − j)θ): the absolute positions cancel.
The cached k is already rotated, and base 10000 is the knob: NTK-aware scaling gives 20,220 at d = 128 and s = 2; YaRN scales logits by 0.967 at s = 2 and 0.910 at s = 8.
ALiBi adds no positional vector: per-head slope m_h = 2^(−8h/n), eight heads from 1/2 down to 1/256.
Subtract m_h|i − j|: 50 at 100 tokens for m = 1/2, 0.39 for m = 1/256. No knob, and far scores fall linearly with no periodic ambiguity.

figures.title: One reservation, two pool sizes
figures.caption: Admission reserves the same 32,786 positions per stream either way: the 32,768-token reply budget plus 16 batch rows plus 2 reserved rows. The equal share of the pool grows with the pool, so the ceiling left for a prompt grows with it. At a quarter pool the share is 65,536 and the ceiling 32,750; at the full window the share is 262,144 and the ceiling 229,358, seven times the first.
figures.alt: Grouped horizontal bars at one scale. Top group, pool of 262,144 positions across 4 streams: equal share 65,536, reservation 32,786, ceiling 32,750. Bottom group, pool of 1,048,576 positions: equal share 262,144, the same reservation 32,786, ceiling 229,358. The reservation bar is identical in both groups; only the share and the ceiling move.

groups.label: pool at 262,144 positions (a quarter of the window)

data.note: 262,144 / 4 = 65,536 and 65,536 − 32,786 = 32,750. 1,048,576 / 4 = 262,144 and 262,144 − 32,786 = 229,358, which is 229,358 / 32,750 ≈ seven times the first ceiling. The reservation does not shrink as the pool grows.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to split the quarter pool, then watch the same reservation leave a far larger ceiling at the full window.

steps.label: 262,144 positions across 4 streams gives each stream 65,536.
The ceiling a prompt sees is 65,536 − 32,786 = 32,750.
Raise the pool to 1,048,576 and the share becomes 262,144.
